summary.headline: Q4 FY26 net revenue INR239 crores, EBITDA up 13% to INR40 crores at 17% margin; proprietary IMFL volumes up 37% YoY.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 net revenue was INR239 crores, with EBITDA up 13% YoY to INR40 crores (17% margin, up 200 bps) and PAT up 5% to INR24 crores (10% margin). Proprietary IMFL, the main growth driver, posted 37% volume growth and a record 22% segment EBITDA margin, while the Inbrew shift from licensing to contract manufacturing kept FY26 top-line growth flattish. Ethanol volumes fell 35% YoY on industry oversupply, and merchant ENA volumes rose 129%. Management guided to FY27 EBITDA margin of around 15% and double-digit consolidated revenue growth, and announced the acquisition of SDF Industries, a Kerala distillery-cum-bottling unit.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever quarterly margin for own-brand IMFL

financial_highlights.value: INR62 crores; volume 9.8 lakh cases; EBITDA margin 20%
Revenue INR24 crores; volume 4 million litres; EBITDA margin 10%
Revenue INR47 crores; volume 6.9 million litres; margin 14%

financial_highlights.change: Up from INR137 crores in FY25 (about 30-35%)

segments.name: Proprietary IMFL
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 6.6 lakh cases (+37% YoY), revenue INR50 crores (+38%), EBITDA margin 22%. FY26 proprietary IMFL revenue INR177 crores; Central Province portfolio grew about 28% YoY.

segments.name: IMIL
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 9.8 lakh cases, revenue INR62 crores (+7% YoY), EBITDA margin 20%. Inbrew moved from IMFL licensing to contract manufacturing, which reduced licensing-linked top line.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR24 crores, volume 4 million litres (-35% YoY) on industry oversupply and lower OMC allocation; EBITDA margin 10% in Q4 and about 7% for the year. Segment EBIT was a loss of INR6.5 crores in Q4 and INR2.5 crores for FY26, per an analyst's reading of the segment disclosure.

segments.name: Merchant ENA
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 6.9 million litres (+129% YoY), revenue INR47 crores (+128%), margin 14%. ENA production rose to 50 million litres from 47 million litres last year on plant efficiency.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of around 15%; management said this would be held in FY28 as well, with a slight increase from FY29.
FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 10%-plus (double digit); IMFL proprietary growth of 30%-plus was also cited, and later 25-30% proprietary volume growth.
FY28 and FY29 growth expected to be higher (about 15% value growth from FY28) on single malt launch; first single malt in FY28 with premium single malt around end-FY28 or Q1 FY29.
Long-term target: proprietary IMFL to reach around 50% of top line (excluding ethanol) in 4-5 years.
IMFL proprietary margin expected at 15%-17% as marketing spend rises with premium portfolio; marketing may reach about 10% of revenue later.
Tequila launch targeted in H1 FY27 (delayed by shipping issues); brandy also planned for FY27; RTD soft-launched in Madhya Pradesh.
Malt sourcing savings expected from H2 FY27 as internally made malt replaces purchased malt.
Kerala target of 2 million cases a year (about 1.6-1.7 million cases currently) with SDF acquisition; ethanol volumes expected to recover if blending rises above 20%.
capex_capacity: Acquired SDF Industries Limited (Kerala distillery-cum-bottling unit) announced 16 April 2026 for about INR30 crores; INR10 crores capex planned for modernisation and automation in FY27 (management corrected analyst's INR70 crores figure).
Commissioned a 6,000 KLPD malt facility; malt maturing in barrels with results ahead of expectations.
ENA production raised to 50 million litres from 47 million litres through plant efficiency and reduced downtime.
Previously bottled via tie-ups at three third-party units with operational challenges; SDF is intended to give in-house bottling control and stable supply.
Ethanol plant is standalone and sells to OMCs; management exploring private oil companies as additional buyers.
demand_pricing: Proprietary IMFL present in 12-14 states; Madhya Pradesh and Kerala are the main contributors; Maharashtra entry limited to premium brands (Hillfort and above) due to MML policy, present in about 3-4 locations (Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Nagpur).
Orange CP Vodka reached about 25% category share in Madhya Pradesh within six months of launch.
Kerala market share 7.3% at FY26 close (management said 1.5% was the share gained last year); third-largest private player in Kerala.

Kultur RTD (8% ABV, 300 ml can, MRP INR130) soft-launched in MP in five flavours; label registrations for other states expected in 1-1.5 months. Management cited Bacardi Breezer with 80-85% RTD share.
Hillfort sold about 4,000 cases and Nicobar about 2,000 cases in FY26.
Packaging cost inflation (PET, paper, aluminium) linked to the war; mitigated via value engineering (removed a mono carton on some popular SKUs) and price increases where possible.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for ethanol decline and new opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: Decline attributed to industry oversupply and lower allocation. Management is pursuing OMCs plus private oil companies and expects volume recovery if blending rises from 20% to 22-25%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the war affecting the business and what is the FY27 EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Main impact is higher packaging costs, not consumption; transport costs may rise if petrol prices rise. FY27 EBITDA guidance is about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ethanol loss-making at EBIT and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ethanol is a non-core, economies-of-scale play with about 7% EBITDA for the year; strategy is to run the plant efficiently, add buyers and improve procurement. Management did not directly dispute the segment EBIT loss.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and margin guidance for FY27 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated growth of 10%-plus in FY27, with IMFL growing 30%-plus. FY28 growth higher (about 15%) with single malt; margin expansion expected from FY29 rather than FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How will the IMFL proprietary margin trend from 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 15%-17% as marketing spend rises with premium launches; marketing may reach about 10% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Kultur details and RTD competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Kultur is 8% ABV, MRP INR130 per 300 ml can, priced around INR1,300 per EDP case; no revenue guidance given for RTD yet.

qa_highlights.question: Single malt timing and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: First single malt in FY28 (management corrected an earlier H2 FY28 statement, then said FY28), premium variant around end-FY28 or Q1 FY29; two price points planned.

risks_watch: Margin dilution: the IMFL margin is guided to fall from 22% to 15-17% as marketing rises; the 15% consolidated EBITDA guidance depends on this.
Packaging inflation (PET, paper, aluminium) and possible transport cost increases if petrol prices rise.
Ethanol remains loss-making at EBIT level; volume depends on government blending policy (20% to 22-25%) and allocation.
Tequila launch delayed by shipping issues; target now H1 FY27.
Inbrew shift to contract manufacturing reduces licensing revenue; top-line growth flattish in FY26.
Kerala 2 million case target and SDF integration execution.
Management answered some questions inconsistently on timelines, including the single malt launch (FY28 vs H2 FY28/FY29) and the capex figure, so these need confirmation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on proprietary IMFL growth and Kerala expansion, but cautious on near-term margins, which management guided down to about 15% for FY27. Answers on ethanol profitability were deflecting, and several timelines (single malt, tequila, capex) were corrected or restated during the call.

We have planned around 10% double-digit growth, 10% plus revenue growth for next year, '27.
So right now, we were doing a bottling tie-up at three different units, okay?
We are targeting to achieve 2 million cases this year annually.

adds.what: SDF Industries Kerala distillery-cum-bottling unit acquired (Kerala target 2 million cases/yr vs ~1.6-1.7 million cases now)
ENA production raised to 50 million litres from 47 million litres via plant efficiency
Single malt launch, first product in FY28 (premium single malt around end-FY28 or Q1 FY29)

growth.why: Management guided FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 10%-plus and proprietary IMFL volume growth of 25-30%, backed by Kerala SDF acquisition (2 million case target vs ~1.6-1.7 million now), a 6,000 KLPD malt facility, tequila launch in H1 FY27 and Orange CP Vodka momentum, though no order book or detailed capacity timeline was given beyond these items; EBITDA margin guided to ~15% vs 17% in Q4.
